slides.speaker_notes: This deck summarizes the operational playbook for OpenZigs tailored for a CTO. It covers prerequisites, installation, authentication, the Next.js Web UI, agent orchestration patterns, sidecars, security, and recommended deployment practices. Use this as a high-level guide to evaluate adoption, plan rollout, and delegate implementation tasks to engineering teams.

content.title: OpenZigs: Platform Overview & Operational Playbook
content.subtitle: Install, Secure, and Scale Autonomous Agent Workflows

slides.speaker_notes: Section 1: Prerequisites. Capture soft and hard requirements up front to avoid wasted integration time. This includes runtime versions, optional media sidecars, and external API keys. Confirm platform support (macOS Apple Silicon preferred for full media capabilities) before planning production deployments.

Key dependencies: modern Node and pnpm for package management; a Copilot subscription is required for SDK/BYOK integration. FFmpeg and image tools are mandatory for media pipelines; Whisper and other model files must be downloaded. Note platform differences: Apple Silicon enables full media sidecars; Linux/Windows provide core features but limited local media capabilities unless using WSL2 + GPU.

image.prompt: dark tech server rack, minimal aesthetic, teal accent lighting, modern datacenter, cinematic studio lighting, high detail
image.alt: Stylized dark server rack with teal accents

slides.speaker_notes: Installation is straightforward for engineering teams: clone, install, configure .env, then run pnpm setup to complete OAuth/device authentication flows. For production, build both backend and UI. Docker compose is available but experimental ΓÇö recommend native pnpm workflow for stability during initial rollouts. Ensure .env is stored securely and CI secrets are injected through your secrets manager.

content.heading: Installation & First Run
content.left:
Clone and install:
ΓÇó git clone https://github.com/openzigs/openzigs.git
ΓÇó cd openzigs
ΓÇó pnpm install
Configure environment:
ΓÇó Copy .env.example ΓåÆ .env
ΓÇó Populate required keys (preserve names)
ΓÇó Run pnpm setup to authenticate
content.right:
Start servers (dev):
ΓÇó Terminal 1: pnpm dev (backend)
ΓÇó Terminal 2: cd ui && pnpm dev (UI)
Defaults:
ΓÇó Backend: http://localhost:3000
ΓÇó UI: http://localhost:3001
Production:
ΓÇó pnpm build && pnpm start (backend + UI)

slides.speaker_notes: On Windows prefer native Node.js for core features and WSL2 for media sidecars that require Linux/GPU. WSL2 + CUDA enables AI media sidecars on compatible NVIDIA GPUs. Be aware of sidecar port assignments and media-ctl.ps1 tool to toggle shared ports like lipsync and music studio. Provide this guidance to desktop ops and developer onboarding materials.

image.prompt: developer workstation running Windows Terminal, stylized, dark UI, teal highlights, clear actionable vibe

slides.speaker_notes: Authentication leverages an OAuth device flow (example: GitHub). The CLI emits a short device code and URL for browser authorization. Tokens persist in the user home directory with strict file permissions. Document organizational security policies around token management and rotation; consider CI/service account flows for headless runners.

Section: Web UI overview. The Next.js application centralizes daily operations: chat, admin, gallery, director studio, task monitoring, scheduler, and pitch tools. Emphasize the admin and audit surfaces for SRE and security teams, and the scheduler/outbox for social publishing automation.

Highlight the Chat UX and Smart Input productivity features: slash/autocomplete triggers for prompts, tools, models and skills. Admin provides BYOK provider config and tool approval controls ΓÇö critical for governance. Tasks page and the visual DAG enable real-time monitoring and troubleshooting of background pipelines. Pitch and Director are high-value features for content and marketing teams.

content.heading: Core UI Routes & Key Features
content.left:
Dashboard ΓÇö system snapshot, approvals
Chat ΓÇö streaming AI chat, model selector
Workbench ΓÇö Markdown editor, file browser
Admin ΓÇö models, tools, brand voice, MCP
Library ΓÇö saved prompts & pipelines
Scheduler ΓÇö cron jobs, dry-run preview
Tasks ΓÇö background agents, visual DAG
Director / Gallery / Pitch ΓÇö media studio
content.right:
Key capabilities:
ΓÇó Smart Input (IntelliSense triggers)
ΓÇó Approval overlays for risky tools
ΓÇó Visual workflow graph & task tree
ΓÇó Skill-aware tool scoping and hot-reload
ΓÇó Media studio: capture, trim, AI director
ΓÇó Pitch composer: script ΓåÆ brand slides

slides.speaker_notes: This comparison is crucial when designing orchestration patterns. Use In-Session agents for low-latency, cost-sensitive tasks that don't require persistence. Use Background agents for durability, auditability, and long-running workloads. Default safeguards exist (max depth, spawn limits) ΓÇö adjust them via Admin for your risk profile.

Closing summary and recommended next steps for a CTO:
1) Validate platform prerequisites (Apple Silicon for full media capabilities where needed).
2) Plan secret management and Cloudflare Tunnel + Access for secure public exposure.
3) Pilot with native pnpm dev workflow and small background agent workloads; instrument sentinel for early alerts.
4) Combine Skills + Library prompts + Scheduler to prototype autonomous pipelines with audit trails.
Reach out to infra and security teams to schedule a deeper technical workshop and a production hardening plan.

metadata.source_script:
Overview / Table of Contents
- Major sections: Prerequisites; Installation; First-Time Authentication; Using the Web UI (Chat, Smart Input, Approval Prompts, Dashboard, Admin, Skills, Library, Scheduler, Workbench, Tasks, Agent Switching, Visual Workflow Graph, Studio, Pitch); Advanced (Agent Chaining, Session Lifecycle, Memory, Tool Limit Configuration, etc.); Platform-specific guides (Windows, Docker, Cloudflare Tunnel); Productivity & Social Media Tools; Media/Director Studio; Configuration Reference; Troubleshooting; Security; feature-specific modules (Sentinel, Knowledge Manager, Social Brain, Secret Vault, SEO tools, Media Queue, Lip Sync).

Prerequisites
- Required software:
  - Node.js 22+
  - pnpm 10+
  - GitHub Copilot Subscription (Individual or Business) ΓÇö SDK access; agent authenticates via OAuth device flow using @github/copilot-sdk
  - Recent Chrome (for browser-read / browser-navigate tools)
  - ffmpeg (media conversion; extract 16 kHz WAV for transcription)
  - ImageMagick + Ghostscript (scanned PDF OCR fallback)
  - Whisper model files (whisper-node ΓÇö install via pnpm exec whisper-node download)
  - Docker Desktop (optional; experimental)
- Platform support:
  - macOS (Apple Silicon): Full Support including AI sidecars (Audio, Image Gen, Music, Video)
  - macOS (Intel): Partial ΓÇö core features; AI sidecars require Apple Silicon
  - Linux: Core Features (native Node.js; AI sidecars unavailable)
  - Windows: Core Features (native Node.js; AI sidecars unavailable without Apple Silicon)
- Optional API keys / env vars (exact names preserved): BRAVE_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, TUNNEL_TOKEN, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, SOCIAL_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN, INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN, INSTAGRAM_BUSINESS_ACCOUNT_ID, FACEBOOK_PAGE_TOKEN, FACEBOOK_APP_ID, FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET, FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID, TIKTOK_CLIENT_KEY, TIKTOK_CLIENT_SECRET, TIKTOK_ACCESS_TOKEN, GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, JDBC_URL, DB_PASSWORD, QUEUE_CALLBACK_URL, PORT=3000, CHROME_DEBUG_HOST, CHROME_DEBUG_PORT, and others referenced.
- Native MCP Server prerequisites (optional): Python 3.10+, Java 17+/JBang, platform API credentials per server; each MCP has its own virtualenv under external/.

Installation
- Clone and install:
  - git clone https://github.com/openzigs/openzigs.git
  - cd openzigs
  - pnpm install
- Configure environment:
  - Create .env at repo root from template; populate required keys (preserve names).
  - Example keys: GITHUB_CLIENT_ID, BRAVE_API_KEY, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, CHROME_DEBUG_HOST=localhost, CHROME_DEBUG_PORT=9222, TUNNEL_TOKEN, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=/path/to/service-account-key.json, QUEUE_CALLBACK_URL, PORT=3000, and commented social API keys.
- Start server:
  - Development:
    - Terminal 1: pnpm dev (backend)
    - Terminal 2: cd ui && pnpm dev (Next.js UI) ΓÇö Next.js UI default: http://localhost:3001
  - Production:
    - pnpm build && pnpm start; UI: cd ui && pnpm build && pnpm start
  - Docker (experimental): docker compose up -d
- Defaults:
  - Backend API: http://localhost:3000
  - Next.js UI: http://localhost:3001
- Note: Docker deployment is experimental; native pnpm dev recommended.

Windows Installation (native Node.js; WSL2 for AI sidecars)
- Quick Install (PowerShell):
  - Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openzigs/openzigs/main/install.ps1" -OutFile "install.ps1"
  - .\install.ps1
- Manual via winget:
  - winget install --id OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS -e
  - winget install --id Git.Git -e
  - npm install -g pnpm
- Then clone, copy .env.example ΓåÆ .env, edit, run pnpm dev and cd ui && pnpm dev; UI at http://localhost:3001
- Uninstall: .\uninstall.ps1 or remove %USERPROFILE%\.openzigs and docker compose down -v
- Windows feature notes:
  - With WSL2 + CUDA sidecars, all AI media features available with NVIDIA GPUs.
  - Many sidecars use specific ports: flux (5005), audio (5006), ltx (5007), imgproc (5008), music (5009), lipsync/studio (5010). LipSync and Music Studio share 5010 ΓÇö only one runs at a time; use media-ctl.ps1 to switch.

First-Time Authentication
- Run: pnpm setup
- CLI prints device code & URL (example https://github.com/login/device, code ABCD-1234); authorize in browser.
- Token saved to ~/.openzigs/auth.json with permissions 0600; persists across restarts.

Using the Web UI (Next.js app)
- Primary routes and purposes:
  - Dashboard: / ΓÇö system snapshot, pending approvals, audit log
  - Chat: /chat ΓÇö AI chat with streaming, model selection, approval overlays
  - Workbench: /workbench ΓÇö rich Markdown editor + file browser
  - Admin: /admin ΓÇö channel config, sidecar management, tool toggles, env status
  - Library: /library ΓÇö saved prompt templates with {{variable}} interpolation
  - Scheduler: /scheduler ΓÇö cron-based job scheduling with prompt linking and model overrides
  - Tasks: /tasks ΓÇö monitor background agent tasks, sub-agents, scheduled work
  - Social Brain: /social ΓÇö unified social inbox, CRM, automation rules, AI auto-replies
  - Models / Capabilities: /admin/models ΓÇö LTX worker introspection, pooled VRAM, per-model limits, sidecar errors
  - Gallery: /gallery ΓÇö asset gallery; inline creation studio for txt2img, img2img, txt2video, img2video, txt2music
  - Director: /director and /director/studio/[id] ΓÇö AI video production wizard, timeline studio, capture & trim
  - Music Studio: /music-studio ΓÇö Voice2Voice pipeline & Smart Remix Lab
  - Pitch: /pitch ΓÇö AI slide deck composer and editor
  - SEO Suite: /seo ΓÇö site audits, gap analysis, exports

Chat (UX & controls)
- Access: http://localhost:3001/chat
- Elements:
  - Model selector; reasoning effort selector (dot-based) for reasoning-capable models (examples: o1, o3, o4-mini)
  - Provider badge when non-Copilot BYOK provider active
  - Context fuel gauge with hover token count; pulses during compaction
  - Session context bar: session ID, context gauge, turn count, session age, compaction status
  - Message input: IntelliSense autocomplete, file attachment, drag-and-drop
  - Real-time streaming responses (word-by-word)
  - Interactive clarification prompts: radio choices or free-text mid-execution

Smart Input (IntelliSense)
- Triggers and categories:
  - / ΓåÆ Prompts (Library templates)
  - # ΓåÆ Tools (enabled MCP tools)
  - @ ΓåÆ Models (available Copilot models)
  - ! ΓåÆ Skills (AI skill personas)
- Keyboard shortcuts:
  - /, #, @, ! to open autocomplete; Γåæ/Γåô navigate; Enter select; Escape dismiss; Shift+Enter new line; Arrow Up at start cycles history.
- Selecting inserts item at cursor (e.g., #web- then select web-search).

Approval Prompts & Global Tool Approval Lock
- High-risk tool calls (write file, run shell) surface approval overlay showing tool name and explanation; Approve or Deny ΓÇö first approval from any connected channel wins.
- Admin ΓåÆ Tools supports per-tool global approval lock (≡ƒöÆ) ΓÇö locked tools always require human approval even if auto-approved elsewhere.
- API toggle example to lock/unlock provided (curl POST to /api/admin/tools/<tool>/global-approval).

Dashboard
- Snapshot stats: total enabled tools, pending approvals, active sessions
- Pending approvals inline approve/deny
- Audit log: filterable tool calls, auth events, system changes; CSV export

Admin (consolidated configuration)
- Channels: configure Telegram, Discord tokens; toggle channels; set default model
- AI Personality: configure system instruction and pre/post prompts; modes: append or replace; Brand Voice indicator when active
- Brand Voice: paste samples separated by ---; AI extracts tone and rulebook; multiple voices storable; active voice injected into video storyboards, social replies, blog-to-video pipelines
- Model Configuration: default reasoning effort (Low/Medium/High/xHigh), BYOK providers (OpenAI, Azure, Anthropic, Ollama, Custom) with test connection; Background Task Default Model setting
- Task Engine: adjust max concurrent background agents (1ΓÇô10), live queue stats, configure tool limit per request (1ΓÇô128)
- Custom Agents: create/edit agent archetypes with name, display name, system prompt, tool allowlist, auto-invoke toggle; shown as cards with tool badges
- MCP Servers: view/manage native MCP servers (social, documents, personal assistant); local servers defined by command/args/cwd/env; HTTP/SSE servers by URL/headers; live running status
- Tools: toggle tools, view risk level badges (≡ƒƒó low, ≡ƒƒí medium, ≡ƒö┤ high); Global approval lock toggle

Environment
- Status grid shows which env vars are configured vs. missing

Skills ΓÇö overview & usage
- Skills: specialized AI personas (agentskills.io SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter), loaded via Copilot SDK skillDirectories; handle tool selection, error recovery, workflow orchestration.
- Skills vs Tools vs Prompts:
  - Skills: passive AI personas always loaded; auto-activate when domain matches
  - Tools: callable functions for power users
  - Prompts (Library): reusable templates with variables; pair with Suggested Skill for repeatable workflows
- Available skills (examples): Media Director, Remix Engineer, Platform Manager, Content Creator, Knowledge Curator, System Operator, Research Synthesizer
- Skill page: each skill card shows icon, name, "Loaded" status, tool badges, rules, example prompts; hot-reloaded via copilot.addSkillDirectory()
- Skill-aware behavior:
  - Tool scoping: skill's allowed-tools + 6 essential tools are sent to LLM
  - Auto-approval: skill tools merged into session auto-approve list
  - Background tasks inherit same behavior
- Creating custom skills: place SKILL.md under src/skills/<skill-name>/; restart server or rely on hot-reload; keep SKILL.md < 500 lines recommended
- Skill Editor (Admin): create new skill with starter SKILL.md template, live validation, ask AI help in editor
- Using skills in chat: automatic activation or explicit ! trigger; /skill-name syntax selects skill

Library (Saved Prompts & Pipelines)
- Features:
  - Create/edit/search prompts with {{variable}} placeholders
  - Preferred Tools restrict tools; Pipeline Stages attach multi-stage pipelines with per-stage prompts, tool restrictions, model overrides, timeouts, auto-approve tools, post-actions
  - Model Override per stage
  - Use as System Prompt; Export/Import via .openzigs-template.json
  - Template autocomplete: type {{ for built-in vars (today, now, day_of_week, month, year)); live preview and validation
  - From Template: create from built-in Pipeline Template Gallery
  - Schedule directly from prompt (Scheduler pre-fills)
- Pipeline Stages per-prompt:
  - Two creation modes: Workflow Wizard (AI generates stages) or Manual Editor (React Flow)
  - Per-stage fields: Name, Prompt, Tools, Auto-Approve Tools, Timeout (default 300s), Post-Action
  - Stage and tool count badges appear on prompt cards

Post-Action Registry (plugin system)
- Post-actions: deterministic actions after stage completion (create-github-issues, send-webhook, etc.); each action type registered with JSON Schema (configSchema); UI renders dynamic config forms
- Built-ins: create-github-issues, send-webhook; REST endpoint GET /api/admin/post-actions returns types
- Create custom post-actions in Admin ΓåÆ Post-Actions or via REST; persisted at ~/.openzigs/custom-post-actions.json; can register programmatically with postActionRegistry.register({...})

Pipeline Template Gallery
- Built-in templates: Research & Summarize, Code Review Pipeline, Content Creation, Competitive Analysis, Monitor & Alert
- Custom templates creatable via POST /api/admin/pipeline-templates; stored at ~/.openzigs/pipeline-templates.json

Scheduler (cron-based jobs)
- /scheduler supports jobs with name, cron expression, action (prompt, shell, pipeline, custom, outbox)
- Link a saved Library prompt and set template variable values
- Features:
  - AI Scheduler Assistant (gpt-5-mini) to describe schedules in plain English
  - Cron preview, Visual Cron Builder (Simple/Advanced)
  - Skill selector auto-populates from Suggested Skill
  - Dry-Run Preview shows resolved prompt, token estimate, tool scoping, pipeline stages
  - Execution History with expandable run details
  - Auto-Approve Tools per job (autoApproveTools) bypass normal approval gating and record audit entries tool_auto_approved
- Template Variables: saved prompts with {{variable}} show input fields in job form; values stored in actionPayload.variables and applied each run
- Built-in dynamic variables: {{today}}, {{now}}, {{day_of_week}}, {{month}}, {{year}} (formatted examples provided)
- Create from Library: /scheduler?createFrom=promptName pre-fills job form
- Outbox action type for scheduled social publishing integrated with Universal Publisher skill and Outbox queue; support Review Required toggle and multi-platform publishing
- Job completion notifications: send to Telegram/Discord when configured

Tasks (Background Agents) & Visual Workflow
- /tasks page: real-time monitoring of background agents; queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled statuses; expand to see spawned sub-tasks
- Token cost badges color-coded: <10k green, 10kΓÇô50k yellow, 50kΓÇô200k orange, >200k red; API endpoints GET /api/tasks/<id>/usage and /api/tasks/usage/summary?hours=24
- Visual Workflow Graph (React Flow + dagre): interactive DAG with status, model, duration, result preview; auto-refreshes every 10s
- Task Tree View: collapsible hierarchy with status icons and per-node duration/token count; API: GET /api/tasks/<id>/tree?maxDepth=10
- Task lifecycle: queued ΓåÆ running ΓåÆ completed | failed; cancel via POST /api/tasks/<id>/cancel
- Persistence: tasks persisted in SQLite agent_tasks with WAL mode; results survive restarts and reconnect notifications via Socket.IO

Agent Switching, Subagents & Orchestration
- Agent Selector in chat to choose specialized agent (researcher, coder, writer); switching resets SDK session
- In-Session subagents (SDK-native) vs Background spawn-agent:
  - In-Session: shares parent session, blocking inline, does not survive page close, cost-efficient (single premium request)
  - Background: independent session, asynchronous, persists in SQLite, survives disconnects, consumes additional premium requests
- Subagent Live Progress Panel shows agent cards, mode badge (In-Session blue / Background amber), tool call log, token usage and elapsed time
- Orchestration Templates: pre-built multi-agent definitions; Admin ΓåÆ Orchestration Templates to execute with variables; REST API for list/create/execute
- Modes: Task (default ΓÇö separate background tasks) vs Session (single SDK session with enableSubagents); choose per execute modal, template default, Scheduler, or REST API; system default is "task"
- Inline Result Injection: background sub-agent results auto-injected as system message back into parent chat
- Safeguards: max recursion depth default 5, max children per parent 10, max spawns per minute 20

Agent Chaining Patterns & examples
- spawn-agent: create AgentTask with parameters goal, context, notify_user, model; used for fire-and-forget, fan-out/fan-in, manager-worker patterns
- orchestrate-agents: parallel agents with mode task|session, agents array, aggregation_prompt, timeout_seconds
- Examples provided: Morning Briefing (cron spawns three parallel agents), Manager-Worker (spec ΓåÆ coder chain), spawn-agent fan-out/fan-in, and detailed parameter behavior

Session lifecycle & infinite context
- SDK sessions cached per conversation ID; resumeSession() attempted on reconnect, infinite sessions enabled by default with automatic context compaction
- Config defaults (excerpt): historyWindow: 20, maxToolsPerRequest: 30, infiniteSessions.enabled: true, backgroundCompactionThreshold: 0.80, bufferExhaustionThreshold: 0.95
- Admin panel: App Sessions and Copilot SDK Sessions with resume, replay, delete, analytics counters for sessions created/resumed/destroyed and compaction counts

Agent Memory (persistent, GitHub-backed)
- Purpose: persistent cross-session memory injected into Copilot sessions; modes: Automatic (LLM-driven save-memory) and Manual via Admin ΓåÆ Agent Memory
- Setup: configure GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in .env, Admin ΓåÆ Agent Memory ΓåÆ Create Memory Repository (creates private repo, default openzigs-memory)
- Memory tools: save-memory, recall-memories; memory injected as markdown grouped by category
- Config sample: memory.enabled, memory.owner, memory.repo, memory.cacheTtlMs (default 300000)
- API endpoints for memory CRUD and status

Tool limit configuration & per-entity tool scoping
- Problem: 90+ tools consume tokens via schema; default cap prevents context bloat
- Essential Tools (6, always included): read-file, list-directory, web-search, shell-execute, spawn-agent, orchestrate-agents
- Contextual Tools (12, included when budget allows)
- Default maxToolsPerRequest: 30 (Admin slider 1ΓÇô128); resolve algorithm: entity allowlist Γê¬ essential tools Γê⌐ enabled tools
- Per-entity scoping: Scheduled Job allowedTools, Saved Prompt preferredTools, Chat message tools; examples for API and Socket.IO usage

Models & BYOK Providers
- BYOK provider support through copilot.provider: openai, azure, anthropic, ollama, custom; Admin API to set provider or clear to revert to GitHub Copilot
- Ollama setup summary:
  - Requires NVIDIA GPU, recommended models gemma4:e4b (9.6 GB, 12 GB+), gemma4:e2b (7.2 GB)
  - Install Ollama (winget/curl), pull model ollama pull gemma4:e4b, configure provider in Admin and select model; test connection via POST /api/admin/models/test-connection
- vLLM support notes: local vLLM provide an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint; auto-detection and API key generation; ensure GPU coordination with image sidecars

Workbench (Project Editor)
- /workbench Markdown editor with file sidebar, WYSIWYG editor, status bar; CodeMirror for syntax highlighting
- Import documents via MarkItDown MCP tool (Office, PDF, HTML, images OCR, audio transcription); prerequisite: MarkItDown MCP server (Python 3.10+)
- File sandboxing: allowedDirs and NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKBENCH_ROOT configurable
- Keyboard shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl + S; unsaved changes indicated

Studio: Director Mode, Capture & Trim, Pitch (AI Slide Decks)
- Capture & Trim: in-browser recorder with system audio and microphone options, VU meter, lossless FFmpeg trims, keyboard shortcuts (R, P, Esc), macOS screen-record permission note
- Video Library & Trimmer: trim (lossless stream copy) and blade mode for splitting; AI Smart Cut analyzes redundancy with frame extraction+Whisper and Vision LLM; Apply All exports clean video
- Director: produce-video tool, templates, voiceover, Remotion v4 render engine; render quality presets and Ken Burns defaults
- Pitch (Studio ΓåÆ Pitch): convert script/brief into brand-consistent slide decks, editable in-browser, export formats PDF/PPTX/ZIP/MD/notes PDF; rate limits per-IP for draft/condense/regenerate/export; prompt-injection envelope and XSS/CSP protections
- Condense pipeline for large scripts: map-reduce with chunk size ~30 KB, CONDENSE_MAP_CONCURRENCY = 4; limits: source_script persisted capped at 50 KB, file upload hard ceiling 2 MB
- Subtitle export SRT/VTT for drafts; Brand Kit system with MCP tools and shared kits

Creative Studio, Gallery & Image Tools
- Gallery image actions: edit produces new asset; resize, crop, filter, convert, watermark, remove background (rembg sidecar), upscale (Real-ESRGAN) ΓÇö sidecars required for remove background & upscale
- Creative tools: QR code generator, Caption Generator, Hashtag Generator, Art Style Picker via MCP tools
- Inpainting Studio: mask-based inpainting with Flux Kontext (Apple Silicon only) ΓÇö requires Mac Mini image-gen sidecar
- Creative Tools REST endpoints under /api/admin/creative

Music Studio & Smart Remix Lab
- Music Studio: Voice2Voice pipeline (Demucs stem separation, Seed-VC voice conversion, final mixdown), Remix Lab for stem separation, AI instrument replacement, auto-mastering (Matchering/ITUR loudness)
- Sidecar for music: ACE-Step sidecar (port 5009) with model downloads on first use; Seed-VC models auto-download
- Waveform DAW view with real-time effects chain via Web Audio API; Uploads and reference management for voice profiles

Media Queue, Worker Nodes, Sidecars & Networking
- Media Queue dispatches image/video/music jobs to GPU worker nodes; workers callback to QUEUE_CALLBACK_URL or detected LAN/public tunnel
- Common sidecar ports: flux 5005, audio 5006, ltx 5007, imgproc 5008, music 5009, lipsync/studio 5010
- Docker: docker compose up -d for full stack; persistence via ~/.openzigs/ host mount; development compose mounts source code
- Cloudflare Tunnel: provides public HTTPS URL for webhooks and OAuth redirects; prefer named tunnel in production; quick mode available for dev (not for production)
- System LaunchDaemon example for macOS cloudflared; Tunnel security recommendations (Cloudflare Access)

Presenter Mode, Multiplayer & A/V Chat
- Presenter Mode converts Director videos into interactive learning experiences with quizzes, Q&A blackboard, and PDF recap; Presenter REST and Socket.IO APIs provided
- Invite-based watch parties: host generates JWT invite links, guests redeem tokens and join /room/<presentationId>; host controls playback, guests are synced read-only
- Multiplayer features: synchronized playback, push-to-talk, P2P voice via PeerJS, mesh video for up to 5 participants, A/V Chat full-duplex with host Voice Pipe mixing and room:audio_chunk events; config and troubleshooting provided

Security & Secret Vault
- Secret Vault stores AES-256-GCM encrypted vault at ~/.openzigs/vault.enc with 0600 perms; secrets referenced as {{SECRET:uuid}} opaque tokens; get-secret returns reference tokens resolved at browser-navigate handler
- Cloudflare Access recommended when exposing agent over tunnel; protect admin except explicit bypass paths (webhooks, health)
- API auth: Bearer token in ~/.openzigs/config.json auth.token or OPENZIGS_TOKEN env var; UI uses NEXT_PUBLIC_OPENZIGS_TOKEN
- Input validation & limits: JSON body 1 MB, chat messages 10,000 chars, file uploads 25 MB/file max 10 files, prompt templates 100,000 chars
- SSRF protection: blocks private IP ranges and cloud metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254
- Post-Action scripts run sandboxed with restricted env variables (OPENZIGS_CONFIG_*) and stripped server env
- Error redaction: internal paths stripped from 500 responses

Knowledge Manager (Local RAG)
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation using LanceDB embedded vector DB; ingest ~/.openzigs/knowledge, chunk, embed (all-MiniLM-L6-v2), watch for changes
- Supported file types: .md, .txt, .pdf, .docx, .pptx, images, media (.mp4/.mp3), code, JSON, CSV, HTML
- Media ingestion: ffmpeg extracts audio, sidecar for transcription; timestamped transcript citations included in results
- Search modes: hybrid (default), vector, fts; API POST /api/admin/knowledge/search; dedup via SHA-256 hashing; visibility levels public/internal/private

Social Brain & MCP Social Integrations
- Unified inbox/CRM across Twitter/X, LinkedIn, YouTube, Reddit, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok with AI auto-replies, comment-to-DM automation, publishing tools
- MCP servers required per platform (Python 3.10+ venv under external/); each platform has specific env vars and setup steps (examples: TWITTER_BEARER_TOKEN, YOUTUBE_API_KEY, LINKEDIN_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, REDDIT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET + credentials)
- Automations: keyword/regex-based DMs, AI-generated rules, approval queue for AI replies, push notifications to Telegram/Discord/Web
- YouTube upload quota warning: videos.insert costs 1,600 units; default quota 10,000 units/day (~6 uploads/day)
- Platform-specific notes for Instagram/Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, Reddit, LinkedIn provided; use Cloudflare Tunnel for webhooks

Firecrawl SEO Suite & Site Auditing
- Firecrawl sidecar (Docker) provides JS-rendered crawling; enables seo-site-audit, knowledge-ingest-website, schema/meta generation, competitive monitoring
- /seo UI with Audit, Links, Content, Performance, Export; reports saved to ~/.openzigs/seo-reports/{domain}/
- Health Score calculation, Core Web Vitals integration, exports to CSV/JSON/PDF; configuration and troubleshooting summarized

Sentinel ΓÇö Autonomous System Monitor
- Background daemon monitoring OpenZigs health: task success rates, stuck/slow tasks, prompt quality, RAG health; alerts via Socket.IO and optional external channels
- Default settings: enabled true, model gpt-4o-mini for audits, checkIntervalMinutes 15, digestHour 9, consecutiveFailureThreshold 3, queueDepthThreshold 10
- Daily digest includes task metrics, token burn, prompt recommendations, saved to ~/.openzigs/sentinel/status.md when persistMarkdownDigest true

Troubleshooting ΓÇö selected items
- Common fixes:
  - GITHUB_CLIENT_ID missing ΓåÆ set in .env and run pnpm setup
  - Empty model selector ΓåÆ Copilot SDK not authenticated (pnpm setup)
  - browser-read connection refused ΓåÆ launch Chrome with --remote-debugging-port=9222 and set CHROME_DEBUG_HOST/PORT
  - Shell commands blocked ΓåÆ add to shell tool allowlist or require approval
  - Sidecar errors (ECONNREFUSED) ΓåÆ start corresponding sidecar or Docker service
  - Scheduled job not firing ΓåÆ ensure scheduler running and job enabled (GET /api/jobs)
  - Gmail, YouTube, social API auth specifics summarized per-platform

Advanced: Local Sidecars, vLLM, Ollama & BYOK
- Local audio sidecar (port 5006) for Kokoro and Whisper; Python 3.12+ for local voices; models download on first request
- vLLM and Ollama options for local LLM hosting; vLLM provides OpenAI-compatible endpoint and auto-BYOK detection; Ollama useful for Gemma models with GPU requirements
- Switching providers clears cached SDK sessions; test connections via Admin APIs

APIs & Examples (selected)
- Task APIs: GET /api/tasks, GET /api/tasks/<id>, POST /api/tasks/<id>/cancel
- Post-actions: GET /api/admin/post-actions; Register via postActionRegistry.register
- Pitch export endpoints: GET /api/admin/pitch/decks/:deckId/export.pdf and others
- Director APIs: POST /api/admin/director/blog-to-video, /shorts, /scenes/:idx/regenerate, /files/upload, /assets/placement, /assets/overlay
- Voice APIs: POST /api/voice/speak, GET /api/voice/config, GET /api/voice/cache, DELETE /api/voice/cache

Closing notes ΓÇö key operational facts to remember
- Default ports and sidecar ports: backend 3000, UI 3001, flux 5005, audio 5006, ltx 5007, imgproc 5008, music 5009, lipsync/studio 5010
- Default limits & safeguards: maxToolsPerRequest default 30, max task depth 5, max children per parent 10, max spawns per minute 20
- Persistence: auth tokens and session data in ~/.openzigs/, SQLite for prompts/jobs/drafts, media assets under Gallery and Director uploads
- Secure public exposure: use Cloudflare Tunnel + Cloudflare Access and rotate secrets; never leave quick tunnel in production
- For deep workflows combine Skills + Library prompts + Scheduler + Tasks + auto-approve tools to build autonomous pipelines with audit trails and recovery patterns

End of condensed presentation source.

slide.speaker_notes: This deck summarizes the operational playbook for OpenZigs tailored for a CTO. It covers prerequisites, installation, authentication, the Next.js Web UI, agent orchestration patterns, sidecars, security, and recommended deployment practices. Use this as a high-level guide to evaluate adoption, plan rollout, and delegate implementation tasks to engineering teams.

content.title: OpenZigs: Platform Overview & Operational Playbook
content.subtitle: Install, Secure, and Scale Autonomous Agent Workflows

slide.speaker_notes: Section 1: Prerequisites. Capture soft and hard requirements up front to avoid wasted integration time. This includes runtime versions, optional media sidecars, and external API keys. Confirm platform support (macOS Apple Silicon preferred for full media capabilities) before planning production deployments.

Key dependencies: modern Node and pnpm for package management; a Copilot subscription is required for SDK/BYOK integration. FFmpeg and image tools are mandatory for media pipelines; Whisper and other model files must be downloaded. Note platform differences: Apple Silicon enables full media sidecars; Linux/Windows provide core features but limited local media capabilities unless using WSL2 + GPU.

slide.speaker_notes: Installation is straightforward for engineering teams: clone, install, configure .env, then run pnpm setup to complete OAuth/device authentication flows. For production, build both backend and UI. Docker compose is available but experimental ΓÇö recommend native pnpm workflow for stability during initial rollouts. Ensure .env is stored securely and CI secrets are injected through your secrets manager.

content.heading: Installation & First Run
content.left:
Clone and install:
ΓÇó git clone https://github.com/openzigs/openzigs.git
ΓÇó cd openzigs
ΓÇó pnpm install
Configure environment:
ΓÇó Copy .env.example ΓåÆ .env
ΓÇó Populate required keys (preserve names)
ΓÇó Run pnpm setup to authenticate
content.right:
Start servers (dev):
ΓÇó Terminal 1: pnpm dev (backend)
ΓÇó Terminal 2: cd ui && pnpm dev (UI)
Defaults:
ΓÇó Backend: http://localhost:3000
ΓÇó UI: http://localhost:3001
Production:
ΓÇó pnpm build && pnpm start (backend + UI)

slide.speaker_notes: On Windows prefer native Node.js for core features and WSL2 for media sidecars that require Linux/GPU. WSL2 + CUDA enables AI media sidecars on compatible NVIDIA GPUs. Be aware of sidecar port assignments and media-ctl.ps1 tool to toggle shared ports like lipsync and music studio. Provide this guidance to desktop ops and developer onboarding materials.

slide.speaker_notes: Authentication leverages an OAuth device flow (example: GitHub). The CLI emits a short device code and URL for browser authorization. Tokens persist in the user home directory with strict file permissions. Document organizational security policies around token management and rotation; consider CI/service account flows for headless runners.

Section: Web UI overview. The Next.js application centralizes daily operations: chat, admin, gallery, director studio, task monitoring, scheduler, and pitch tools. Emphasize the admin and audit surfaces for SRE and security teams, and the scheduler/outbox for social publishing automation.

Highlight the Chat UX and Smart Input productivity features: slash/autocomplete triggers for prompts, tools, models and skills. Admin provides BYOK provider config and tool approval controls ΓÇö critical for governance. Tasks page and the visual DAG enable real-time monitoring and troubleshooting of background pipelines. Pitch and Director are high-value features for content and marketing teams.

content.heading: Core UI Routes & Key Features
content.left:
Dashboard ΓÇö system snapshot, approvals
Chat ΓÇö streaming AI chat, model selector
Workbench ΓÇö Markdown editor, file browser
Admin ΓÇö models, tools, brand voice, MCP
Library ΓÇö saved prompts & pipelines
Scheduler ΓÇö cron jobs, dry-run preview
Tasks ΓÇö background agents, visual DAG
Director / Gallery / Pitch ΓÇö media studio
content.right:
Key capabilities:
ΓÇó Smart Input (IntelliSense triggers)
ΓÇó Approval overlays for risky tools
ΓÇó Visual workflow graph & task tree
ΓÇó Skill-aware tool scoping and hot-reload
ΓÇó Media studio: capture, trim, AI director
ΓÇó Pitch composer: script ΓåÆ brand slides

slide.speaker_notes: This comparison is crucial when designing orchestration patterns. Use In-Session agents for low-latency, cost-sensitive tasks that don't require persistence. Use Background agents for durability, auditability, and long-running workloads. Default safeguards exist (max depth, spawn limits) ΓÇö adjust them via Admin for your risk profile.

Closing summary and recommended next steps for a CTO:
1) Validate platform prerequisites (Apple Silicon for full media capabilities where needed).
2) Plan secret management and Cloudflare Tunnel + Access for secure public exposure.
3) Pilot with native pnpm dev workflow and small background agent workloads; instrument sentinel for early alerts.
4) Combine Skills + Library prompts + Scheduler to prototype autonomous pipelines with audit trails.
Reach out to infra and security teams to schedule a deeper technical workshop and a production hardening plan.
